newsitem.title: GERMANY: German debt and futures optimism set to continue.
newsitem.headline: German debt and futures optimism set to continue.

text.p: German DTB Bund futures powered ahead on Friday to reach dizzy heights, with dealers saying the strength and speed of the rally fed market optimism that the climb could continue next week.

Dealers said there were no fundamental reasons for the rally, but said hopes for lower interest rate had crept back into the market following comments by France's monetary policy council member Jean-Pierre Gerard that short-term interest rates should be cut in Germany and France.
The December Bund future ended at 102.53, up 83 ticks, after earlier reaching an all-time high of 102.59.

Traders spoke of the possibility of a rate cut to help the fulfilment of criteria required for European monetary union, by weakening the French and German currencies and boosting exports. "Sooner or later the Bundesbank will cut rates for monetary union reasons, to help France," said one dealer.
Traders said nobody wanted to be left on the sidelines in the rally, but added that next week the release of important economic data would influence the market's direction.
Dealers said they would be watching the release of German GDP data on Wednesday, as well as the German October industrial production figures for signs of recovery in the economy.
The release of U.S. employment data on Friday will also provide a focus.
The 10-year April Bund reached a high of 104.50, up from 103.57 on Thursday, with its yield at 5.61 percent.
The average yield of public issues sank 10 basis points to a historical low of 5.10 percent.
